clue.text: One state cooperating with another? There are strings attached

definitions.note: a clause standing for the adverb: something done with strings attached is done only on terms

parts.note: a state or situation is a condition, as in 'in good condition'
an ally is one cooperating with another, especially a nation in wartime

explanation.surface: A question about one nation siding with another, answered by the cynical remark that every alliance has its price.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a clause standing in for an adverb: when there are strings attached, a thing is given only on terms.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings attached are terms or provisos, so an offer with them is made only on terms, not freely.

clue.text: About a penny added to poultry

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
P is the abbreviation for a penny in British money
added on, so ON

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts roughly a penny on the price of chicken.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table, a kind of poultry.

clue.text: Champion said to suffer defeat late in the day?

indicators.note: said tells us to take the word as it is spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a knight was a champion who fought for a cause or lady
to fall is to be defeated, as a city falls

explanation.surface: A champion is beaten when the contest runs late.
explanation.walkthrough: KNIGHT and NIGHT are pronounced alike, the K being silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Dusk, the coming of darkness, arrives late in the day; the question mark admits the loose phrasing.

clue.text: I dash into road in the country

indicators.note: into says the word for dash goes inside the road abbreviation

parts.note: elan is dash or flair

explanation.surface: Someone describes darting out onto a road somewhere abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a nation, an example of a country.

clue.text: Trouble for harlots in street, ultimately

indicators.note: to trouble the words is to stir them up, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Street walkers eventually run into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means as a final option when all else fails, so eventually or finally.

clue.text: Several in action destroyed doing this?

definitions.text: Several in action destroyed doing this?

indicators.note: destroyed tells us the phrase is smashed up and its letters rebuilt

explanation.surface: A grim remark about conscripts: several who were in action were killed while serving.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: young men conscripted into the forces could be sent into action and killed.
explanation.definitionFit: Compulsory military duty for young men, as in postwar Britain, could put conscripts into combat.

clue.text: Mostly noisy group scowling

indicators.note: Mostly means all of the word but its final letter

parts.note: noisy means loud
a ring is a group or gang, as a spy ring

explanation.surface: A rowdy gang glowering at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To lour or lower is to frown sullenly, so the participle is a synonym for glowering.

clue.text: Former pupil and youngster, the reverse of such a lout?

indicators.note: the reverse of tells us to read the two pieces together from the end backwards

parts.note: OB stands for old boy, a former pupil of a school
a youngster is a boy

explanation.surface: An old boy and a lad are said to be the very opposite of a hooligan.
explanation.walkthrough: Old boy then boy, read backwards as one string, gives the answer; the surface claims they are a lout's opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobbo is British slang for a rowdy, uncouth young man, a synonym for lout.

clue.text: Wine experts initially expect tiny amount to drink, nothing more

parts.note: pros are professionals, experts

indicators.note: initially tells us to take only the opening letter of expect

parts.note: cc, a cubic centimetre, is a tiny measure of liquid
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Wine buffs expect only a sip at a tasting, nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosecco is a sparkling white wine from north-east Italy.

clue.text: Paint FBI agents into a hole

indicators.note: into tells us the agents go inside the hole

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
G-men, government men, is slang for FBI agents

explanation.surface: A gangster's instruction to bury the federal agents in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment is colouring matter, and paint is loosely called by that name.

clue.text: Writer is regularly bleary at end of day

indicators.note: at end of says these letters come after the day

parts.note: Thur is short for Thursday

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of bleary, starting with the first

explanation.surface: An author is worn out and blurry-eyed when the day's work is done.
explanation.definitionFit: James Thurber was an American humorist, cartoonist and author of The Secret Life of Walter Mitty.

clue.text: Canute's mad — he's quite mad

definitions.note: a clause standing for a noun: someone of whom it is said that he is crazy

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of the king's name go wild and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A verdict on King Canute, who in legend ordered back the tide: he was off his head.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the 's of Canute's supplies a letter S. Canute was an 11th-century English king, mocked in a famous story for commanding the sea to retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutcase is informal for a lunatic, a person thought crazy.

clue.text: Sinister order in America restricting head of organisation

indicators.note: restricting means the first group of pieces hems in the next letter

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
taken as written
US is the United States, America

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of organisation

explanation.surface: A shady secret society in the US keeping its leader under wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means threatening or foreboding, so it is a synonym for sinister.

clue.text: Food for committee members

definitions.meaning: ... means meals provided, as in ... and lodging
a body of directors or committee members

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both daily meals supplied to a lodger and a governing body of directors.

clue.text: Short body Morse hacked in quarters

indicators.note: hacked means chopped about, so the letters are rearranged
Short means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: bod is slang shortening of body, a person

explanation.surface: The TV detective Morse cuts up a corpse in his lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims BODY to BOD; 'hacked' scrambles BOD plus MORSE. Inspector Morse was a British TV detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarters means lodgings or rooms where people sleep, and the answer names such rooms.

clue.text: A single amount to begin with treated cold?

definitions.text: A single amount to begin with treated cold?

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters are rearranged
to begin with means the first letter of amount

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A patient takes one dose of medicine at the start to deal with a cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a painkiller might be one dose taken to ease a cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An analgesic is a painkilling drug, such as one a sufferer might take for a cold.

clue.text: Untidy person creates trouble in county, standing on head

indicators.note: in says the trouble sits inside the county
in a down clue, standing on its head means the county is read upside down, bottom to top

parts.note: Worcs is the abbreviation for Worcestershire, an English county
care is worry or trouble

explanation.surface: A scruffy lout makes a nuisance of himself in the shires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'creates' is only a link here. 'standing on head' reads the county abbreviation upward, giving SCROW, and 'in' places the trouble after its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shabbily dressed is figuratively compared to a straw figure set up in a field to frighten birds.

clue.text: Clothes store's entered by 20, say

indicators.note: entered by means the store word has the name placed inside it

parts.note: a deli is a delicatessen store, plus S from the 's

indicators.note: say tells us to take the name as it is pronounced

parts.note: the answer to 20 is the title figure of The Taming of the Shrew, whose heroine is called Kate

explanation.surface: A clothes shop is invaded by an ill-tempered woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is the answer to 20-down; Kate is the shrew of Shakespeare's comedy, and CATE is spelt to sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Delicates are fragile garments such as lingerie, washed on a gentle cycle.

clue.text: Composer found orchestra leaders drowned by string player? No way

indicators.note: drowned by means submerged in, so placed inside
No means the abbreviation for way is taken out

parts.note: a cellist plays a stringed instrument
ST, street, is a way
the leading letters of orchestra, its first two

explanation.surface: A composer finds his orchestra's leaders drowned out by a cellist, with no escape.
explanation.definitionFit: Arcangelo Corelli was an Italian Baroque violinist and composer.

clue.text: Tea company in South America, it's plain

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: A tea firm operating in South America is said to be unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gran Chaco is a vast lowland plain spanning Paraguay, Bolivia and Argentina; 'in South America' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chaco is a hot semi-arid lowland region in central South America, a geographical example of a plain.

clue.text: White powder — look — carried by beast of burden

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the animal

parts.note: a camel is a beast of burden
lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: Someone points out a white powder being smuggled on a pack animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Calomel is mercurous chloride, a white powder once used as a purgative.

clue.text: Pay close attention to verbose characters

indicators.note: characters means the letters of verbose are used as the pieces of a new word

explanation.surface: Advice to listen carefully to long-winded people.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch or note closely, a synonym for paying close attention to.

clue.text: Mostly clever mousy creature

indicators.note: Mostly means all of the word but its last letter

parts.note: shrewd means clever or astute

explanation.surface: A sharp-witted little rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a small insect-eating mammal that looks like a mouse.

clue.text: Hairdresser uses them to produce curls and waves

definitions.text: Hairdresser uses them to produce curls
definitions.meaning: cylinders round which hair is wound to set curls
long heavy sea waves breaking on shore are called this

explanation.surface: A stylist uses curlers to create curls and waves in hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' seems to be part of the hairstyling picture, but it is the second definition: big ocean swells.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both hair curlers and long swelling breakers at sea.

clue.text: Promise special clothing

parts.note: wear means clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: A vow to wear particular clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear is to vow or pledge solemnly, a verb synonym for promise.

clue.text: Cherry is edible growth, large and round

parts.note: a morel is an edible fungus
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A cherry is described as a big round fruit that can be eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a dark sour cherry used in cooking and preserves.

clue.text: Some swimmers expected to get soaked

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people in the pool were expecting to get wet.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse is to plunge into liquid, so to drench or get soaked.

clue.text: Tale-teller finding teacher in playground at break?

definitions.meaning: someone who exposes wrongdoing, telling tales on their employer
the duty teacher signals the end of playtime by sounding a whistle

explanation.surface: A sneak is found out to be the teacher on playground duty.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: the teacher literally blows a whistle at break time.
explanation.definitionFit: An informer who exposes wrongdoing, and literally a person who sounds a whistle.
